title: select-serial-port: portName is device basename instead of full path on Linux, causing SerialPort.open() → NetworkError
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.

### Electron Version

41.0.3

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Ubuntu

### Operating System Version

Linux Mint 22.3 (Ubuntu 24.04, kernel 6.8.0-110-generic)

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

Unknown

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

In the `select-serial-port` IPC event, `portList[n].portName` should be the **full device node path**: `/dev/ttyUSB0` (or `/dev/ttyACM0`, `/dev/cu.usbserial-*` on macOS, etc.).

### Actual Behavior

`portName` contains the **device basename** (e.g. `ttyUSB0`) instead of the full device node path (`/dev/ttyUSB0`). Chromium uses this stored path when `port.open()` is subsequently called, so it attempts to open the file `ttyUSB0` relative to the working directory, which fails with `ENOENT` → `NetworkError: Failed to open serial port`.

The user is a member of `dialout`, the device exists at `/dev/ttyUSB0`, and the same Web Serial code works correctly in Chrome and Chromium browsers.
